headline: Fed Day: Rates Hold Steady as Oil Climbs Again
tileReason: The daily 30-year average held at 7.33% Tuesday; oil is rebounding this morning and all eyes are on the Fed's 2:00 PM ET decision.
takeaway: Mortgage rates were unchanged again on Tuesday. The daily 30-year average held at 7.33% for a third straight session, still near its lowest level in a month. Bonds had another calm day, with the 10-year Treasury yield, which mortgage rates tend to follow, closing just under 5%. This morning the yield is up slightly, to about 5.01%, as oil climbs back after two days of declines: Brent crude is up roughly 1.5% to around $116 a barrel on reports that Washington is weighing new strikes on Iran after next week's elections and on continued Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites. Pricier oil feeds inflation worries, which nudges rates up. Some lender surveys that update overnight show rates a little lower than last week, so pricing looks roughly flat to slightly higher today. The big event is this afternoon. The Federal Reserve (the Fed, the central bank) announces its decision at 2:00 PM ET, and Chair Warsh speaks at 2:30. Markets see about a 90% chance the Fed holds steady but price a strong chance of a hike in December, so his tone matters more than the decision. Then comes a busy Thursday: the PCE inflation report (the Fed's preferred inflation gauge) and the first estimate of third-quarter economic growth. Microsoft and Alphabet also report earnings after today's close, which can shift money between stocks and bonds. Over the next month the odds look close to balanced, with a slight lean toward rates staying about where they are.

fedOdds.title: Odds of a Fed hike on Oct 28
fedOdds.source: CME FedWatch via Paralia Trading Desk and AirdropAlert (Oct 28); Kiplinger live blog (Oct 26); KuCoin News/Reuters poll (Oct 28)
fedOdds.note: On decision morning, CME FedWatch puts the chance of a hike today at about 10%, so roughly 90% for a hold (Paralia Trading Desk and AirdropAlert, Oct 28); Kiplinger had 90.6% for a hold Monday afternoon. Sources differ on December: one Oct 28 note cites about 80% odds of a hike by December, while others citing FedWatch show about 73%. A Reuters poll found 94 of 100 economists expect no change today and all expect a December hike. The decision is at 2:00 PM ET.

drivers.title: Oil rebounds on Iran strike reports
drivers.text: After two days of declines, Brent crude is up about 1.5% this morning to roughly $116 a barrel. Reports say Washington is weighing a short military campaign against Iran after the midterm elections and has asked Gulf allies to prepare, and Houthi attacks on Saudi energy sites continue. Higher oil prices raise the risk that inflation stays high, so investors demand more from bonds, which pushes yields and mortgage rates up. Reports that Qatar gave Iran a new draft deal are limiting the gains.

drivers.title: Fed decision today, December hike in view
drivers.text: The Fed is widely expected to hold its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4.00% at 2:00 PM ET, but markets still see a good chance of a hike in December after hot September inflation. That expectation keeps a floor under bond yields and mortgage rates. If Chair Warsh sounds more worried about inflation than expected, rates could rise this afternoon; if he sounds patient, they could ease.

drivers.title: Inflation and growth data due Thursday
drivers.text: Forecasters expect September's core PCE inflation (which leaves out food and energy) to tick up to about 3.1% from 3.0%, and third-quarter growth is expected to come in stronger than the second quarter's 2.2%. Investors are positioning cautiously ahead of those numbers, which tends to keep yields from falling much. A hotter result would add pressure on rates; a softer one would bring relief.

drivers.title: Tech earnings could move money between stocks and bonds
drivers.text: Microsoft and Alphabet report after today's close. Last week's selloff in tech stocks sent money into bonds and helped pull mortgage rates to a one-month low. Improving confidence in AI has eased some of that safe-haven buying this week, but a disappointing report could send investors back into bonds, which would help rates.

drivers.title: Mortgage rates are still unusually far above Treasuries
drivers.text: The Optimal Blue conforming 30-year index is running about 2.20% above the 10-year Treasury yield (as of Oct 26), versus a long-run average of about 1.76%. That extra cushion means mortgage rates have room to improve if markets calm down, even without a further drop in Treasury yields.

outlook.basis: It's close to a coin flip, with a slight lean toward rates staying about where they are. Working in borrowers' favor: nervous tech stocks can send money into bonds on short notice, diplomacy with Iran is still alive, and mortgage rates are still unusually far above the 10-year Treasury (about 2.2% vs. a long-run average near 1.76%). Working against them: a December Fed hike is still widely expected, September inflation ran hot, PCE inflation is forecast to tick up, and oil is back near $116 with reports of possible U.S. strikes on Iran. Big swing events: today's Fed decision and press conference, Thursday's PCE inflation and GDP data, the November 3 midterm elections, the November 6 jobs report, the November 10 CPI report, and any escalation in the Gulf.
outlook.caveat: This is professional judgment from 30+ years watching these markets, not a guarantee. One oil headline or data surprise can move rates a quarter point in a day.

talkingPoints.buyers: The daily 30-year average is about 7.33%, near a one-month low and down from roughly 7.5% in early October. Today's Fed decision and Thursday's inflation data could bring bigger swings than usual, so it's worth asking your lender how locking, a float-down option, or waiting would each fit your closing date.
talkingPoints.sellers: Buyers are still stretched at rates above 7%, and new home sales beat forecasts in September, so resale homes are competing with builders. Realistic pricing, or a seller credit buyers can use to lower their rate, can help a home stand out.
talkingPoints.oneLiner: Mortgage rates are steady around 7.33%, near a one-month low, heading into this afternoon's Fed decision and Thursday's inflation data.
